title: Math-mode includes reference nonexistent text.tex(.latex) contexts (begin-end-commands, greeks, math-characters, math-numerics)
description:
**Math-mode LaTeX includes reference context names that don't exist in Sublime's bundled LaTeX syntax, so highlighting inside `$...$`/`$$...$$` math blocks silently degrades.**

`Quarto.sublime-syntax` includes several `text.tex`/`text.tex.latex` sub-contexts for math-mode rendering:

```yaml
- include: scope:text.tex.latex#verb
- include: scope:text.tex.latex#text-decorators
- include: scope:text.tex.latex#references
- include: scope:text.tex.latex#begin-end-commands
- include: scope:text.tex#greeks
- include: scope:text.tex#math-brackets
- include: scope:text.tex.latex#boxes
- include: scope:text.tex#math-commands
- include: scope:text.tex#math-operators
- include: scope:text.tex#math-characters
- include: scope:text.tex#math-numerics
- include: scope:text.tex.latex#general-constants
```

Four of these — `text.tex.latex#begin-end-commands`, `text.tex#greeks`, `text.tex#math-characters`, `text.tex#math-numerics` — don't exist in the bundled LaTeX package that ships with current Sublime Text (checked directly against `TeX.sublime-syntax` and `LaTeX.sublime-syntax` from the built-in `LaTeX.sublime-package`, Sublime Text 4215). Sublime prints a console warning and silently drops each missing include rather than failing loudly, so any Quarto document with a LaTeX math block loses part of its math highlighting with no visible error to the user — only a console message:

```
no such context scope:text.tex.latex#begin-end-commands at line 1802 column 16 of atom(2)
no such context scope:text.tex#greeks at line 1803 column 16 of atom(2)
no such context scope:text.tex#math-characters at line 1809 column 16 of atom(2)
no such context scope:text.tex#math-numerics at line 1810 column 16 of atom(2)
```

**Reproduced live** (Sublime Text 4215, Windows, installed via Package Control, version 1.0.2): installing the package and letting Sublime generate its syntax summary (which validates every `include:` against the actual installed target syntax) produces exactly these 4 warnings, repeated for each math-mode context block in the syntax file. The rest of Quarto's highlighting (YAML front matter, fenced code blocks with embedded languages, inline code, markdown formatting) works correctly — this is isolated to the LaTeX math-mode includes.

**Suggested fix:** these context names look like they were written against a different (possibly older, possibly a third-party) LaTeX syntax package than the one Sublime Text currently bundles. Worth checking what context names the currently-targeted LaTeX package actually exposes for greek letters / math characters / numerics / begin-end commands (some of this content might now live under different names, e.g. as part of a combined `math-*` context) and updating the includes to match, or vendoring the specific rules needed instead of depending on the exact internal context names of another syntax.

title: Syntax highlighting of included files with _ prefix
description: The [Includes](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/includes.html) section of Quarto's docs says: > Note that we use an underscore (`_`) prefix for the included file. You should always use an underscore prefix with included files so that they are automatically ignored (i.e. not treated as standalone files) by a `quarto render` of a project). However, my text editor appears to parse this syntax as an error. I am using Sublime Text Build 4152 with version 1.0.2 of this package. I suspect the issue stems from the use of balanced underscores to italicize/emphasize text in Markdown syntax (e.g., `_this text_` becomes _this text_). I've skimmed through parts of [Quarto.sublime-syntax](../blob/main/Quarto.sublime-syntax) but could not identify where/how to address this issue. These syntax definitions are unfamiliar territory for me. FWIW: The content from the included files are rendered properly. The issue is limited to qmd's syntax highlighting.

title: Add quarto renderer functionality (code in the issue)
description:
Hello,

I built a very simple command to render quarto documents from Sublime. I was thinking of publishing the package myself by I think it makes more sense if it's maintained by you people together with the syntax highlighter. Here's the code:

``` python
import sublime
import sublime_plugin
import subprocess
import os

class QuartoRenderCommand(sublime_plugin.TextCommand):
    def run(self, edit):
        # Get the current file path
        file_path = self.view.file_name()
        
        if not file_path:
            sublime.error_message("Please save the file before rendering.")
            return
        
        if not file_path.endswith('.qmd'):
            sublime.error_message("This is not a Quarto document (.qmd file)")
            return
        
        # Get the directory of the current file
        file_dir = os.path.dirname(file_path)
        
        # Show a status message
        sublime.status_message("Rendering Quarto document...")
        
        # Run the quarto render command
        try:
            result = subprocess.run(['quarto', 'render', file_path], 
                                    cwd=file_dir, 
                                    capture_output=True, 
                                    text=True)
            
            if result.returncode == 0:
                sublime.status_message("Quarto document rendered successfully")
            else:
                sublime.error_message(f"Error rendering Quarto document: {result.stderr}")
        except FileNotFoundError:
            sublime.error_message("Quarto CLI not found. Make sure it's installed and in your PATH.")
```

and here's the command:

```json
[
    {
        "caption": "Quarto: Render Document",
        "command": "quarto_render"
    }
]
````

Let me know if you're interested!
